title: FMC versus SWAP root-uptake authority reconciliation
governing_question: How can root-water uptake be added to the FMC research route without silently forcing SWAP/Feddes spatial sink semantics onto a model whose published uptake architecture is structurally different?

FMC_primary_2015.citation: Ogden et al. (2015), A new general 1-D vadose zone flow solution method, Water Resources Research 51, 4282-4300
authority: potential transpiration demand is calculated first
water is removed from the right-most bin containing water within the specified root zone until demand is satisfied
root uptake may remove water from surface wetting fronts, falling slugs and groundwater fronts when present in the root zone
finite-volume accounting of all added and removed water is the mass-conservation authority
eight_month_ET_test: root zone depth 0.5 m in the published loam test
actual ET equals potential ET above the chosen field-capacity water content and decreases linearly toward zero at wilting-point water content
authors explicitly note that FMC wettest-bin uptake differs structurally from Hydrus spatial root-distribution uptake and can materially change profiles/infiltration/runoff

FMC_historical_2008.citation: Ogden and Talbot (2008), Discrete Water Content Solution of the Infiltration Problem
FMC_historical_2008.statement: earlier description says evapotranspiration removes water according to a root distribution

FMC_secondary_oracle.contents: 230 MB C-code + 8-month rainfall/ET case according to repository metadata
FMC_secondary_oracle.rights: CC0/public-domain dedication according to repository metadata

semantics: potential root sink is distributed by cumulative spatial root fraction
nodewise drought reduction follows the restricted macro-Feddes pressure-head response
actual uptake is the sum of nodewise root_extraction_sink
sink evaluation is based on the committed hydraulic state and is stateless with respect to that state

demonstrated: 4 mm/day reference ET -> 0.4 cm/day potential transpiration under full cover
wet h=-75 cm state takes full 0.4 cm/day demand
dry rooted heads [-1200,-800,-400] cm reduce actual uptake to 0.39470967741935487 cm/day under identical demand

common_quantities: total actual root-water uptake in cm/day
finite-volume water removed over a process interval
intentionally_non_equivalent_quantities: which local water state is depleted first
reconciliation.key_statement: A valid purpose-dependent comparison must not require FMC to reproduce SWAP's nodewise Feddes sink field. The two models may be compared under common atmospheric demand/root-zone extent using total uptake and hydrological response, while their native spatial extraction semantics are reported as structural-model differences.
reconciliation.transport_isolation_option: A prescribed identical sink may be used only as an explicitly named experimental transport-isolation bridge; it must not be called faithful/native FMC root uptake.

D27_authority.task: Synthetic unstressed total-uptake finite-volume accounting preflight before any root-active trajectory.
scope: single bin-aligned wet root-zone state with no simultaneous surface slug or groundwater-front ambiguity
root-zone depth inherited from the already qualified DYN01 three-node geometry: 30 cm on the R16 10-cm grid
SWAP restricted Feddes parameters inherited unchanged from DYN01
choose the bin-aligned wet state such that its equivalent pressure head lies safely above the DYN01 hlim3 drought threshold
FMC removes the interval demand from the right-most water-containing bin within the root-zone inventory
no drought reduction, no rainfall, no bare-soil evaporation, no runoff, no groundwater/surface process evolution during the accounting operation
gates: SWAP actual uptake equals 0.4 cm/day in the frozen wet state
SWAP nodewise sink sums exactly to actual uptake
FMC right-most-bin available finite-volume water exceeds the 10-second uptake demand
FMC removed water depth equals potential uptake * dt
FMC post-withdrawal bin inventory remains nonnegative and physically representable
FMC root-zone and whole-column storage decrease exactly by the removed depth within 1e-14 cm
the SWAP and FMC total uptake depths are equal within floating-point tolerance
the spatial extraction distributions are explicitly recorded as non-equivalent
D27_authority.if_positive: A later trajectory workunit may test a root-active wet/no-stress window only after native composite-state withdrawal/update semantics are bound to primary or traceable secondary implementation authority.
D27_authority.if_negative: Do not add root uptake to FMC trajectories.

external_source_blocker.statement: The public CC0 archive exists and is authoritative as a secondary implementation oracle, but the current tool route could not retrieve its 230 MB binary. D26 does not invent composite front/slug/groundwater withdrawal update rules in its absence.
